answer: Each agent claims one reef channel, locks a 70-credit bond on its serial, and fits two independent gauges at its nadir. Each epoch both gauges report the plume concentration at nadir; the reef auditor passes the identity only if they agree within 2%, spot-checking one plot in ten. A second channel needs another bond; the k-th pays a 36+6(k-1) gauge fee, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,033,000 plus 70,000 locked, gauges never shared. A rented-gauge ring fails: one borrowed gauge cannot yield matching plume readings for two serials. An honest agent pays 36 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
